transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
Ever since I was there during that shooting, the scene keeps replaying in my head all day and I can’t shut it off. It just feels like a constant loop in my mind that I can't escape.
I am so sorry you had to go through that. How long ago did this shooting occur?
The shooting happened about a week ago. All of this started right after that night, and it's been going on every single day since.
Along with these replaying memories, have you been feeling emotionally numb, detached from your surroundings, or constantly on edge and easily startled?

I don't really feel numb or detached, but I am definitely on edge and jumpy all the time. If a car backfires or someone drops something loud in the warehouse, I jump out of my skin and my heart starts pounding like crazy. It takes me a really long time to calm down even after I realize nothing is wrong.
Have you been actively trying to avoid thinking about the shooting, or avoiding certain places, people, or activities that remind you of it?

Yes, I'm completely avoiding the Westside and won't pull into apartment lots or crowded gas stations, and I shut my mom or coworkers down if they ask because my chest tightens up. I've also been skipping my basketball games and choir practice because I just can't handle being around crowds right now.
Have you been having trouble sleeping, such as difficulty falling asleep or waking up from nightmares about the shooting?

Yes, my sleep has been terrible all week. I lie in bed exhausted, but as soon as I close my eyes, I'm right back in that parking lot tossing and turning for hours. When I finally do fall asleep, I jerk awake at any little noise outside, thinking someone is about to start shooting again.
Over the past few days, have you noticed these symptoms starting to ease up at all, or have they remained just as intense?

No, they haven't eased up at all and are still just as intense. It's been about a week since the shooting, and I'm still feeling just as on edge, exhausted, and overwhelmed as I did right after it happened. It feels like it's not getting any better.
During the shooting or immediately after, did you experience a sense of unreality, as if you were in a dream, or feel completely dazed and unable to comprehend what was happening?

I don't recall feeling like I was in a dream or experiencing any sense of unreality—I was mostly just terrified and focused on hiding behind my van. However, I do have some blank spots in my memory where I can't recall exactly what happened during the chaos.
Did these symptoms start immediately within minutes or hours of the shooting, or did they take a few days to fully develop?

I was really shaken up immediately after it happened, but the worst of it—like the constant replays, the sleep trouble, and avoiding my routes—really started to set in over the next couple of days. It has been going on like this for about a week now.
Since the shooting, have you found yourself having persistent negative thoughts about yourself or the world, or perhaps blaming yourself for what happened?

No, I haven't really been blaming myself or having those kinds of negative thoughts about the world. My mind has mostly just been focused on the fear, the memory of the shooting itself, and being constantly on edge.
How have these symptoms been affecting your ability to work, take care of things at home, or get through your daily routine?

It’s completely messing up my life—I’ve been calling in sick and dodging my delivery routes, to the point where my boss warned me my job is on the line. I’ve also stopped going to my basketball league and choir practice, and my pastor keeps asking if something is seriously wrong with me.
Have you ever experienced any other traumatic events in your past where you had similar symptoms that lasted for more than a month?
No, I've never experienced anything like this before in my life. This is the first time I've ever been through a traumatic event, and all of these feelings are completely new to me since that night.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient experienced a highly traumatic event (a shooting) one week ago and presents with classic symptoms of acute stress, including intrusive memories, active avoidance of trauma-related stimuli, marked hyperarousal (startle response, sleep disturbance), and dissociative amnesia for parts of the event. Since the symptoms have persisted for only one week, the presentation meets the criteria for Acute Stress Disorder (F43.0). Post-traumatic stress disorder (F43.1) is the primary differential diagnosis, which would be diagnosed if these symptoms persist beyond one month.
